faq.title: Got Questions?
faq.description: Find answers to common questions about our services, treatments, and what to expect during your recovery journey.

faqs.question: Do I need a referral to book an appointment?
faqs.answer: No referral is necessary. You can book directly through our website or by calling our clinic. We welcome self-referrals and work with most health insurance providers.

faqs.question: What should I bring to my first visit?
faqs.answer: Please bring your ID, insurance card, any relevant medical records or imaging results, and a list of current medications. Comfortable clothing is recommended.

faqs.question: How do I schedule an appointment?
faqs.answer: You can book online through our website, call us directly, or use our mobile app. Same-day appointments are often available for urgent cases.

faqs.question: How long does each session typically last?
faqs.answer: Initial assessments are 60 minutes. Follow-up treatment sessions are usually 45-60 minutes depending on your condition and treatment plan.

faqs.question: Is physiotherapy treatment painful?
faqs.answer: Physiotherapy should not be significantly painful. You may experience mild discomfort during treatment as we work on tight or injured tissues, but we always work within your comfort level.

faqs.question: What should I wear to my session?
faqs.answer: Wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothing that allows easy access to the area being treated. For lower body issues, shorts work best. For upper body, a tank top or loose t-shirt is ideal.

faqs.question: Do you accept insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes, we accept most major insurance plans. Contact our office with your insurance information and we'll verify your coverage and benefits before your appointment.

faqs.question: What are your payment options?
faqs.answer: We accept cash, major credit & debit cards and Bank Transfer. Payment plans are available for those without insurance coverage.

faqs.question: Will my insurance cover all treatments?
faqs.answer: Coverage varies by plan. Most insurance covers a certain number of physical therapy visits per year. We'll help you understand your benefits during your first visit.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: This varies widely depending on your condition. Some patients see significant improvement in 4-6 sessions, while chronic or complex conditions may require longer treatment plans.

faqs.question: Will I get exercises to do at home?
faqs.answer: Yes! Home exercises are a crucial part of your recovery. We provide personalized exercise programs and can send video demonstrations to your phone.

faqs.question: Is physiotherapy the same as chiropractic care?
faqs.answer: While there are overlaps, physiotherapy focuses on rehabilitation, movement re-education, and exercise therapy in addition to manual techniques, offering a more comprehensive approach.

faq.title: Common Service Questions
faq.description: Understanding your treatment plan is part of the healing process.

acuteInjuries.question: Which therapy is right for acute injuries?
acuteInjuries.answer: For acute injuries (occurring within the last 48-72 hours), we typically recommend starting with a diagnostic consultation followed by gentle Manual Therapy to manage inflammation and pain before progressing to active rehabilitation.

combineTreatments.question: Can I combine treatments?
combineTreatments.answer: Absolutely. Our approach is holistic. Most successful recovery plans involve a mix of Manual Therapy for immediate relief and Corrective Exercise for long-term prevention.

postOpPackages.question: Do you offer post-op packages?
postOpPackages.answer: Yes. Our Post-Surgical Rehab program is comprehensive. We bundle initial assessments, wound care checks, and a 12-week progressive strength track to get you back to normal life.

sportsRecovery.question: Is sports recovery only for professionals?
sportsRecovery.answer: Not at all. Whether you're a weekend warrior, a daily jogger, or an elite athlete, our Sports Recovery protocols are designed to help any active body recover faster and prevent injury.
